resource.name: aws_s3_bucket_policy
resource.description: Attaches a policy to an S3 bucket resource. Policies can be attached to both S3 general purpose buckets and S3 directory buckets.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_s3_bucket_policy` resource enables the attachment of access control policies to S3 buckets, allowing users to define fine-grained permissions for bucket-level operations. Common use cases include securing data by restricting access to specific IAM roles, accounts, or services, enabling cross-account access, and enforcing compliance with organizational security standards. This resource supports configurations for both general-purpose and directory-style S3 buckets, making it essential for managing access control, integrating with external services, and implementing custom security policies.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_s3_bucket_policy` to allow cross-account access to an S3 bucket by specifying an IAM policy document with a `principals` block for an external AWS account. It illustrates the use of the `aws_iam_policy_document` data source to define permissions for actions like `s3:GetObject` and `s3:ListBucket` on both the bucket and its objects.

arguments.name: bucket
arguments.description: (Required) Name of the bucket to which to apply the policy.
arguments.llm_summary: Specifies the name of the S3 bucket to which the policy will be applied, enabling users to define access control and permissions for the bucket's resources. This argument is essential for associating the policy with the correct bucket, ensuring alignment with security and compliance requirements.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_s3_bucket_policy` resource represents the unique identifier of the S3 bucket policy, typically auto-generated by Terraform. While optional, it can be used to reference or track the policy within Terraform's state, aiding in resource management and ensuring consistency across deployments.

arguments.name: policy
arguments.description: (Required) Text of the policy. Although this is a bucket policy rather than an IAM policy, the `aws_iam_policy_document` data source may be used, so long as it specifies a principal. For more information about building AWS IAM policy documents with Terraform, see the AWS IAM Policy Document Guide. Note: Bucket policies are limited to 20 KB in size.
arguments.llm_summary: The `policy` argument in the `aws_s3_bucket_policy` resource allows users to define the JSON-formatted access control policy for an S3 bucket, specifying permissions, principals, and conditions that govern how the bucket and its objects can be accessed. By setting this argument, users can enforce fine-grained security rules, such as restricting access to specific AWS accounts, services, or IP ranges, and achieve compliance with organizational or regulatory requirements.
